main_body: A small wooden bucket with a dark rim, a short opening holding greenish slop, a handle across it, and an orange-brown banded front face above a dark base.
top_band: Rim at about rows 6-7 (orange-brown, 1-2 px), then a dark and green opening at rows 7-8. There is no clear light top surface several rows tall.
evidence: In the middle column the thin rim at row 6 gives way to a dark and green strip at rows 7-8. That strip is crossed by the handle and is not drawn as an ellipse, so it reads as a flat band and not as an interior seen from above. The front staves at rows 9-13 are painted flat, with no distinct front-edge line or eave shadow. It is a front elevation with a thin rim, so the opening and top surface are not clear enough to pass.

style.evidence: The outline is a dark brown that leans toward the wood, which suits the material. The wood has about 4 tones, with hoops, a green slop patch and some banding. That is thinner than the stall and well references, which have 5-6 steps, per-element texture and richer tiles. The small size and the near-flat staves make it look simpler than the references.
